patients.summary: Teacher with Crohn disease, SLE, mild asthma and iron deficiency anemia who joins in 2019; HHT is named in 2021, a Crohn rectovaginal fistula in 2023 and neuropsychiatric lupus with a seizure in late 2023. Post-abortal choriocarcinoma is treated to remission in 2024; after a 2025 cesarean delivery it returns in July 2026 with brain and lung metastases and she is on chemotherapy at today.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller: Wendy Hastings, DOB 09/05/1989. Wants to transfer primary care here; has been with another practice for years and says the hard part has been getting anyone on the phone between visits. Has Crohn's and lupus, sees GI and rheumatology outside and plans to keep them. Membership terms reviewed, packet emailed. Records release signed electronically for her prior primary care office. New patient visit booked for 9/17 at 8:40, asked to bring all pill bottles and her inhaler.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Summary of records received (41 pages, scanned to media).

Problem list carried by prior office: Crohn's disease (dx 2014, managed by outside GI), systemic lupus erythematosus (managed by outside rheumatology), mild intermittent asthma, anemia on oral iron.
Medications at last visit: mesalamine DR 1.2 g three times daily; hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily; prednisone 10 mg daily; albuterol HFA as needed; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Screening: cervical cytology 2016 negative. Tdap 2016. Influenza vaccine most years.
Last CBC (spring 2019): mild anemia, hemoglobin in the low 11s, platelets normal.
No hospitalizations listed in the prior five years.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

30F elementary school teacher transferring care. Main reason for switching: wants a doctor who answers between visits; her specialists are outside and she would like one person keeping the whole list straight.

Crohn's: diagnosed in 2014 at 24 after months of diarrhea and weight loss. Followed by an outside GI group. On mesalamine 1.2 g TID. Says she is quiet right now, 1-2 formed stools a day, no blood.
SLE: diagnosed some years ago by rheumatology (joint pain and a rash at the time per her account, she does not remember the details). Hydroxychloroquine 200 daily and prednisone 10 daily for a long time; GI and rheum have both bumped prednisone up for flares and brought it back down. Has never been off it for long.
Asthma: albuterol maybe once a month, more with colds. No ED visits for asthma, no oral steroid bursts just for asthma.
Nosebleeds: since she was a kid. Comes and goes, a few a month lately, usually stops with pressure. On iron for low blood count for years, assumed from the nosebleeds. No black stools.

PMH as above. PSH: none. Meds reconciled with bottles (5). NKDA.
FH: mother with lupus. Maternal aunt with rheumatoid arthritis. Father gets frequent nosebleeds, as does a cousin on his side.
SH: lives with partner. Never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks a month, no drugs. Teaches 2nd grade.
GYN: periods regular. Last Pap 2016 normal.

ROS: no fevers, no joint swelling now, no rash now, no chest pain, no dyspnea at rest. Fatigue at the end of school days, chronic.

EXAM: vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT: anterior nares without active bleeding, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abdomen soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds. Joints without synovitis. Skin: no malar rash or discoid lesions today. Neuro grossly normal. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal appearing, Pap with HPV collected.

A/P
1. Crohn's disease - quiet on mesalamine, GI outside. Will request their notes.
2. SLE on HCQ + chronic prednisone 10 - rheum outside. Needs yearly retinal screening for HCQ; she thinks her last eye exam was last winter. Long-term prednisone: will look at bone density.
3. Mild intermittent asthma - albuterol PRN, adequate.
4. Iron deficiency anemia, likely from chronic nosebleeds - CBC and iron studies today, continue ferrous sulfate.
5. Health maintenance: Pap/HPV today. HIV and hep C screening today. Lipids, A1c (steroid exposure), TSH. Flu shot when the supply arrives next month.

Return in about 4 months, sooner by text.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wendy, your labs are back. Hemoglobin is a little low at the level your old office was seeing, and your iron stores are on the low side of normal, so keep taking the iron every day. Kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, sugar and thyroid are all normal. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Urine was clean. Pap is still pending; I'll message when it's in. Nothing needs changing for now.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you! Nice to get this so fast. Will keep up the iron.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came after school for flu vaccine. No fever today, no prior reaction to flu vaccines. Quadrivalent inactivated 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS reviewed. Tolerated, left after 15 min observation. Pap result (normal, HPV neg) reviewed with her at her request.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology clinic - follow-up visit 12/03/2019.

Dear colleague, thank you for letting us know Ms. Hastings has joined your practice. We saw her in routine follow-up for systemic lupus erythematosus. She reports no new rash, no joint swelling, no pleuritic pain. Exam today without synovitis or mucocutaneous lesions. Recent labs reviewed. Disease quiet. Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily and prednisone 10 mg daily; annual retinal screening for hydroxychloroquine (she reports one last winter). Return in 6 months.

Medications: mesalamine 1.2 g TID, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

orders.order: DXA bone density, hip and spine

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine follow-up. Rheum saw her in December, nothing changed. Bowels steady. Albuterol twice since fall, both with a cold in her classroom. Nosebleeds about the same, a few a month. Wants to know if the prednisone is hurting her bones.
O: vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No rash.
A/P: SLE and Crohn's quiet on current regimen. Asthma intermittent, fine. Anemia stable - CBC today. Long-term prednisone 10 mg: ordered DXA. Discussed calcium and vitamin D from diet and weight-bearing exercise. RTC 4-6 months or sooner.

documents.title: Hydroxychloroquine retinal screening
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology - exam 02/11/2020.
Indication: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, annual toxicity screening.
Visual acuity 20/20 OU. IOP normal. Dilated fundus exam normal OU. Automated 10-2 visual fields full OU. SD-OCT macula: normal ellipsoid zone, no parafoveal thinning.
Impression: no evidence of hydroxychloroquine retinopathy. Repeat in one year.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Indication: long-term glucocorticoid therapy, premenopausal. Lumbar spine L1-L4: Z-score -0.4. Left femoral neck: Z-score -0.2. Total left hip: Z-score 0.1. Technically adequate study, no vertebral levels excluded.
reports.conclusion: Bone mineral density within the expected range for age.

documents.title: DXA result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Bone density normal for age. Messaged patient. No treatment needed; recheck only if steroid exposure changes a lot.

documents.title: Is prednisone making me high risk?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: School is remote for now. Should I be doing anything different because of the prednisone and lupus? Should I stop the prednisone? I have about 2 weeks left of everything.

documents.title: RE: Is prednisone making me high risk?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Please don't stop the prednisone on your own - after this many years your body depends on it and stopping suddenly is dangerous. Same for the hydroxychloroquine and mesalamine. Being on prednisone does put you in the group that should be extra careful: stay home as much as you can, masks and hand washing, and let me know right away with fever or cough. I've sent 90-day refills of everything so you have a cushion. Let's do a video check-in in June instead of an office visit.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, patient at home, consented. Finished the school year remotely. Feels well overall. Bowels unchanged. No joint flares. Has used albuterol maybe once since March. Nosebleeds a couple of times a month, stops with pressure. Adherent to all meds.
No exam beyond what's visible: comfortable, speaking full sentences, no rash on face.
A/P: Stable. Labs for monitoring this week at the lab drive-up. Refills current. Flu shot in the fall.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb unchanged at her usual mild anemia. Kidney and liver function normal. No action. Released to portal with a short note.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology - telehealth follow-up 09/01/2020.
Crohn's disease, diagnosed 2014. Currently 1-2 formed stools daily, no bleeding, no abdominal pain, weight stable. No perianal symptoms. Plan: continue mesalamine 1.2 g three times daily; prednisone per rheumatology at 10 mg. Labs reviewed from her primary care office. Follow-up one year or sooner for symptoms.
Meds: mesalamine, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate. NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

Teaching in person with masks, hybrid days. Tired but ok. PHQ-9 3. Sleep fine most nights. Exercise: walks with partner on weekends.
Crohn's quiet per GI in September. Lupus quiet. Albuterol rarely. Nosebleeds: a few a month, one this summer that took about 30 minutes to stop at home.
Meds unchanged, NKDA. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT normal, nares without active bleeding. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin without rash. Joints normal.

Prevention: Pap/HPV normal 2019, next 2024. HIV/HCV done 2019. Flu vaccine today. Eye screening for HCQ done February, normal; next due February.
Labs: CBC, CMP, ferritin, UA.
A/P: Stable chronic disease. Continue all meds. RTC ~4 months.
